text:
maya: heads-up — brought up a new HF checkpoint (v2-smallish) and our eval suite shows systematic truncation + weird attention artifacts.
samir: what do you see in the conversion logs? any config.json oddities?
maya: conversion printed a WARNING about "config fallthrough: max_position_embeddings not set, defaulting to 2048". model.tokenizer.pad_length() > 2048 in some tests so tokens get silently clipped. also HF config had `rope_scaling: {"type":"linear","factor":2.0}` which our converter dropped.
liam: dropping rope_scaling would explain shifted attention phases at long context. that + clipping = hallucinations at the tail.
jen: was num_key_value_heads present? last time mismatch between kv heads and attn heads caused kv-cache index errors during incremental decode.
maya: config.json had "num_key_value_heads": 32 but "num_attention_heads": 64 — so it's fine ratio-wise, BUT HF also had `sliding_window: 256` set which our runtime translates to `prefix_window` incorrectly (we used tokens not pairs), so the sliding window was effectively 128.
samir: oof. so three layers of mismatch: a) max_pos defaulting/cap, b) rope_scaling ignored, c) sliding_window unit conversion bug. any stack traces from the failing evals?
maya: here is the small failing excerpt from the rouge test run:

```
RuntimeError: kv_cache index out of bounds at step 1025 (max_pos 2048)
Trace: attention_mask mismatch -> attention wrap -> wrong cached key offset
```

liam: that stack looks like cached offsets assume original tokenizer positions but runtime used truncated positions. That matches rope scaling gone — phase of rotary embeddings will drift after a wrap.
infra-bot: conversion-runner: job 8792 completed with status WARNING, artifacts at s3://redwood-conversions/v2-smallish/8792/logs.txt
jen: is this reproducible locally with the HF weights + our convert script? maya: yes, I ran `scripts/convert_hf.sh --model v2-smallish --dry-run` and saw the warnings.
samir: quick mitigations: (1) update converter to preserve `rope_scaling` and emit a runtime-compatible field, (2) keep `max_position_embeddings` explicit — prefer model.config.get("max_position_embeddings") or set to tokenizer.model_max_length, (3) fix sliding_window unit (tokens vs chunks).
maya: + add a smoke test that runs a 3k token context passthrough and checks kv-cache indices and embeddings-per-token continuity.
liam: also add an eval that compares prefix logits on long context between HF (PyTorch) reference and our runtime after conversion; small delta threshold. catches rope/scaling problems early.
jen: note on quantization: earlier we saw that 4-bit quant + mismatched kv_heads led to larger accuracy drop. so add quantized pipelines to the smoke matrix.
samir: I'll open a draft PR to the converter with the rope_scaling preservation and max_pos fallback fix. assigning myself. will add tests as follow-up.
maya: thanks. can someone triage whether any hosted models are affected (prod)?
liam: quick grep shows 3 models in catalog with empty max_position_embeddings field. I'll make a tracker issue and flag infra to block rollout until conversion script lands.
infra-bot: incident-tracker: created ISSUE-412 for catalog scan results and blocked rollout tag applied.
jen: small doc note: we should document expected HF config fields we require (max_position_embeddings, rope_scaling, sliding_window, num_key_value_heads) and the converter's mapping rules.
maya: agreed — adding "conversion checklist" item to the onboarding doc.
samir: timeline: PR this week, smoke tests green next week, then catalog re-run.
maya: thanks all. :thumbsup:
